# Valve covers and PCV hose replacement

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Replace both valve covers, clean surfaces around crossing PCV hoses, and install new or cleaned PCV hoses. [t516]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Remove the upper intake plenum to access the valve cover gaskets.
2. [Partial] Stuff rags into the intake runners to prevent debris from falling in during work.
3. [Partial] Replace both left and right valve covers without removing the cam control solenoids if desired.
4. Clean the gasket surfaces carefully around the area where the PCV hoses cross over.
5. Install new or cleaned PCV hoses, including those for the VAIS system on the intake plenum.

_Procedure reported by [t516]._

## Parts

- Cam Solenoid Gasket, Optional x2 (23797-ZA000) [t516]
- Intake Upper Plenum Gasket, x3 (14032-EA200) [t516]
- PCV Hose between Rocker Covers (11826-EA200) [t516]
- PCV Hose from Rocker Cover to Air Intake Tube (11826-ZL80B) [t516]
- PCV Hose to Intake (11823-EA20A) [t516]
- Throttle Body Gasket (16175-EA200) [t516]
- Valve Cover Gasket Left (13270-EA21C) [t516]
- Valve Cover Gasket Right (13270-EA20C) [t516]
- Valve Cover Left (13264-EA210) [t516]
- Valve Cover Right, includes PCV valve (13264-EA200) [t516]

## Tips & gotchas

- Order the PCV hoses at the start of the job rather than waiting for them later. [t516]
- Use Permatex grey RTV sealant at the front corners of the covers to fill gaps where gaskets might not make full contact. [t516]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Assuming aftermarket cam solenoid gaskets are replaceable o-rings when they may be molded suspension bushing types. [t516]
- Forgetting that old PCV hoses can become brittle and crack under pressure from the crossover point. [t516]
